audit_findings.title: The acquisition perimeter is assigned to the wrong fiscal year
audit_findings.magnitude: Acquired revenue was $208.2 million in partial FY2025 and $358.2 million in full FY2026; current anchor is $53.1 million versus FY2026 OE of $115.6 million; mechanically using $115.6 million would raise base value to approximately $41.01 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The fiscal-year error affects the OE anchor by mixing pre-acquisition, partial-year, and full-year observations without correctly identifying the structural break.
audit_findings.evidence: On October 31, 2024, the Company completed the Acquisition at a purchase price of approximately $297.5 million ($286.5 million, as adjusted, net of cash acquired), subject to certain further adjustments set forth in the Purchase Agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated factual error: the October 31, 2024 acquisition occurred during FY2025, making FY2025 partial and FY2026 the first full year. The acquired portfolio is large enough that the old ten-year trend may not represent the enlarged company. Because a mechanical full-year-OE sensitivity crosses the $38.25 market price, the error is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion, although $115.6 million is not itself established as the correct normalized anchor.
audit_findings.action: Correct the perimeter metadata, reconstruct comparable pre- and post-acquisition OE, and rerun the anchor and all scenarios using a normalization method that explicitly accounts for the acquisition discontinuity.

audit_findings.title: Post-year-end plant-closure economics are absent from historical owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Closure, transfer, remediation, replacement-capital, and contract-manufacturing cash flows would enter forecast OE and maintenance or transition capital expenditure; eventual consolidation savings could increase OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In August 2026, management decided to close the Company’s Chicago Heights manufacturing facility as part of a strategic consolidation of our plant network.
audit_findings.explanation: The closure decision occurred after FY2026 and therefore is not a historical-OE error. The filing states that all financial impacts cannot yet be reasonably estimated. Transition costs could reduce value, while consolidation savings could offset them or increase value, so the net direction is unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain management's closure and transfer budget, including severance, remediation, asset write-offs, replacement capital, contract-manufacturing costs, working capital, and recurring savings; rerun projected OE when estimates become available.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may add foreign cash gross of repatriation friction
audit_findings.magnitude: $81.994 million total cash/STI bridge, including $80.0 million held internationally; complete removal equals approximately $1.97 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any nondistributable operating cash or incremental repatriation tax reduces the cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: If amounts are repatriated from certain of our foreign subsidiaries, we could be subject to additional non-U.S. income and withholding taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether all foreign cash is excess and distributable net of tax is unresolved. However, even removing the entire $81.994 million cash bridge—not merely the repatriation friction—would reduce bull value from $21.99 to approximately $20.02 per share, still far below the $38.25 market price. It therefore cannot reverse the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Classify cash by jurisdiction and operating requirement, document distributability, and deduct incremental withholding and income taxes in the bridge; no conclusion-level rerun is required unless other material findings also change the valuation.

audit_findings.title: An accrued tax claim ahead of common equity may be missing from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $21.041 million, approximately $0.51 per diluted share and 2.3%–2.9% of scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: If settlement cash is absent from forecast OE and working-capital assumptions, the accrued claim should reduce the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As tax law is complex and often subject to varied interpretations, it is uncertain whether some of our tax positions will be sustained upon examination.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability is filed, but whether its eventual settlement is already captured in OE remains unresolved. Even deducting the full $21.041 million would reduce bull value only from $21.99 to approximately $21.49 per share, leaving it well below the $38.25 price and not changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace uncertain-tax-position settlements through the OE and working-capital construction; if uncaptured, deduct the expected cash settlement from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: FY2026 earnings contain a nonrecurring tariff-recovery benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.5 million FY2026 cost-of-goods-sold benefit plus $3.2 million deferred in inventory; together $11.7 million, or 22.0% of the $53.1 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The $8.5 million can inflate the FY2026 OE observation and its contribution to the trend anchor; the $3.2 million will reduce cost of goods sold when the affected inventory is sold.
audit_findings.evidence: Of the total recovery, $ 8.5 million related to tariffs on inventory previously sold to customers and was recorded as a reduction of cost of goods sold for the three and twelve months ended June 30, 2026, and $ 3.2 million related to tariffs on inventory held as of June 30, 2026 and was recorded as a reduction of inventory.
audit_findings.explanation: The nonrecurring benefits are demonstrated. Nevertheless, even the deliberately conservative ceiling of treating the entire $11.7 million as permanent recurring anchor inflation would reduce bull value by approximately $4.41 per share, from $21.99 to $17.58, reinforcing rather than reversing the conclusion at a $38.25 market price. The correct impact should be smaller because the amounts are discrete and the anchor is trend-based.
audit_findings.action: Remove the $8.5 million recovery from FY2026 normalized OE, prevent the $3.2 million inventory benefit from entering normalized FY2027 OE, recompute the trend anchor, and rerun scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The forecast may omit an imminent Brazil regulatory cliff
audit_findings.magnitude: $27 million of FY2026 Brazilian virginiamycin sales, equal to approximately 1.8% of total sales and 3.3% of MFA-and-other sales; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Delayed or restricted therapeutic registrations could reduce forecast revenue and margin while adding conversion and compliance costs to projected OE and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: On April 27, 2026, MAPA published an ordinance prohibiting the importation, manufacture, and marketing of antimicrobial feed additives classified as important in human or veterinary medicine, including virginiamycin and bacitracin, for performance enhancement.
audit_findings.explanation: The ordinance and exposed sales are filed facts, but the adverse cash-flow outcome is forward-looking: registrations were in the final stages of review, and the record provides neither product margin nor probable customer retention under therapeutic indications. The valuation effect therefore cannot presently be established.
audit_findings.action: Confirm MAPA approval dates, permitted indications, pricing, expected customer conversion, product-level contribution margin, and compliance costs; immediately rerun forecast OE under delayed-approval, restricted-use, and customer-attrition cases if approval is not secured before the transition expires.
